# Results — Study 63 (Free-Fall): the short-volatility carry, SVXY vs SPY, 2018–2026

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Daily total returns of **SVXY** (short VIX
futures) and **SPY**, Yahoo. SVXY's free history begins 2018-01, which includes the Volmageddon crash —
the defining event. Inputs fingerprint `893091a77c52`.*

## The verdict, earned — Signal `REAL` · Tradability `FRAGILE` · "Naive short-vol survives"? `BUSTED`

Selling volatility earns a `REAL` carry — the volatility risk premium. SVXY compounded at **+11.8%/yr**
and its post-Volmageddon, de-levered version runs **+10%/yr (Sharpe 0.45)**. But it is the textbook
*picking up pennies in front of a steamroller*, so `FRAGILE` and `BUSTED` as a naive hold: skew **−4.8**,
a **−95% drawdown**, and a single **−83% day** on **6 Feb 2018** that vaporised years of carry in hours.
The premium is real and harvestable *if sized and hedged*; bought and held, it blows up.

## Data stamp

- **Pair**: SVXY (short-vol) vs SPY, daily total return, 2018–2026, fingerprint `893091a77c52`

## A real carry — wearing a catastrophic tail

| | CAGR | Sharpe | vol | max-DD | skew |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SVXY (short-vol) | +11.8% | 0.56 | **55%** | **−95%** | **−4.8** |
| SPY (market) | +15.7% | 0.95 | 17% | −34% | −0.3 |

The carry is genuinely positive (+11.8%/yr), but it comes with three times the market's volatility, a
−95% drawdown, and a skew of −4.8 — a return stream that drips up and crashes down. The Sharpe (0.56)
flatters it; the −95% drawdown is the number that matters.

## The steamroller, quantified

| | value |
|---|---|
| median day (the carry being collected) | **+40 bp** |
| worst single day | **−83%** (6 Feb 2018) |
| crash days (<−20%) | **5** |
| cumulative loss across those 5 days | **−95%** |

This is the whole risk in one table. On a typical day you collect ~40 bp of premium; then five days out
of ~2,100 destroyed 95% of the position between them. The −83% on 6 February 2018 ("Volmageddon")
liquidated the original 1× short-vol ETFs entirely. You spend years being paid a little to underwrite a
catastrophe.

## The carry resumes — for those still standing

| post-Volmageddon (de-levered −0.5×) | value |
|---|---|
| CAGR | **+10.0%/yr** |
| Sharpe | 0.45 |

After Feb 2018, SVXY was re-struck at half leverage and the carry resumed: +10%/yr. The premium didn't
vanish — but the episode is the point. A short-vol book makes money right up until it doesn't, and the
"doesn't" is total. The honest way to harvest it is *sized small, with the tail explicitly owned* (cf.
[Study 27 Steamroller](../../27-steamroller/) on FX carry).

## The honest takeaway

The short-volatility premium is `REAL` — selling vol pays a steady carry (+10–12%/yr). But a naive
short-vol hold is `BUSTED`: skew −4.8, a −95% drawdown, an −83% day. It is `FRAGILE` — harvestable only
sized and hedged, never bought and held. The pennies are real; so is the steamroller.
